construct: In skeletal muscle, T-tubule depolarization is sensed by CaV1.1, the dihydropyridine receptor. Conformational coupling between CaV1.1 and the sarcoplasmic-reticulum ryanodine receptor RyR1 rapidly opens RyR1 and releases stored calcium; extracellular calcium influx through CaV1.1 is not required as the trigger in the same way it is in cardiac muscle.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Skeletal-muscle excitation-contraction coupling uses CaV1.1/DHPR as the T-tubule voltage sensor and direct conformational signaling to RyR1 for SR calcium release.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: CaV1.2-RyR2 is a plausible pair because it mediates cardiac excitation-contraction coupling, but the stem specifies skeletal muscle and preserved contraction with negligible extracellular calcium.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Tissue type and calcium-independence of the trigger uniquely select CaV1.1-DHPR and RyR1.
